result.note: Tests the India–France Innovation Roadmap 2030 (June 2026): its mobility and industrial deliverables, the DEPA health-data link, and the February 2026 partnership upgrade.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–France Innovation Roadmap 2030 adopted in June 2026:
items: France aims to welcome 30,000 Indian students by 2030, backed by an expanded Mutual Recognition of Qualifications framework.
The roadmap sets up an aeronautical training campus in Bengaluru.
The roadmap creates a bilateral startup corridor called the InnoXchange Bridge.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The aeronautical training campus is in Kanpur, not Bengaluru. Bengaluru will instead co-host one of two back-to-back space summits with Paris in September 2026.
questions.source: On the industrial front, the deal sets up an aeronautical training campus in Kanpur and a bilateral startup corridor called the InnoXchange Bridge.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, India and France upgraded their bilateral ties to which of the following?
questions.explain: The two countries upgraded ties to a Special Global Strategic Partnership in February 2026 and launched the India-France Year of Innovation 2026, which focuses on AI in health and digital science. The Innovation Roadmap 2030 followed in June 2026.
questions.source: The two countries upgraded ties to a “Special Global Strategic Partnership” in February this year and launched the “India-France Year of Innovation 2026,” focusing on AI in health and digital science.

questions.prompt: Under the India–France Innovation Roadmap 2030 adopted in June 2026, France is matching India's Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) with its own data platforms in which sector?
questions.explain: France is linking its health data platforms with India's DEPA to enable secure, consent-based research sharing. This forms part of the roadmap's focus on Trusted AI, which also covers child safety online and risk-based AI governance.
questions.source: France is matching India’s Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) with its own health data platforms to facilitate secure, consent-based research sharing.
